What blocks an as-is merge in a capability-security repo is one authority leak the report and the proposed comment both misdescribe: `actorRuleset("implement", {role:"reader", …})` keeps the own-namespace glob, so the supposedly read-only tester profile's allowedTools contains `Bash(prx implement:*)` — the very verb (`prx implement agent`) that launches an executor over the plan, i.e. the tester can still re-trigger the implementation the issue complains about. The repo already has the precedent for this exact hazard (`submit` uses `omitOwnNamespace: true` because the glob would re-admit `prx submit publish`), the new test asserts only that Edit/Write are denied and never pins the allowlist, and the ready-to-paste comment says 'reader ruleset (Edit/Write denied, `bun test` + `prx tools git` allowed)' which omits both `Bash(prx implement:*)` and `Bash(bun run:*)`. Fix is one line (`omitOwnNamespace: true`) plus a test pin and a corrected comment; the issue's acceptance criterion (a live doc-only pilot drive reaching review/merge) is honestly reported as not exercised, which the maintainer may also treat as a gate.
